title: Michael Burry just made a surprising call on the Nasdaq 100
detail:
Michael Burry just made a surprising call on the Nasdaq 100
Hillary Remy
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 10:17 AM PST 5 min read
^NDX

Michael Burry was still doubling down against the Nasdaq 100 as recently as Nov. 12. When the index bounced off the 27,000 level that day, he added to his puts and summed up the rally in three words: "Behold the bull-trap," according to TheStreet. Now that bet is gone, and the timing is hard to ignore.

The Nasdaq 100 fell 20% from its October peak on an intraday basis on Nov. 25, officially hitting bear market territory. Burry used the slide to walk away from the trade and lean the other way. For the first time in a while, the investor famous for betting against the housing market holds more long positions than short ones.

The shift is a notable turn for someone who spent much of 2026 positioning for a correction. His next move is already taking shape, and it points squarely at a stock that just had one of its biggest days in more than two decades.

Why Michael Burry walked away from his Nasdaq puts

The puts he just sold were not small. In his Nov. 12 Substack post, Burry doubled his Nasdaq 100 put position with contracts expiring in early 2027 at strikes roughly 20% below the index. He also said he expected a significant correction in chip and tech stocks before mid-2027.

Also read: Michael Burry sees a serious problem Wall Street may be overlooking

He went after chip stocks the same week. Burry bought back part of his VanEck Semiconductor ETF puts and named AMD and Broadcom as possible winners if Nvidia's grip on the market loosens. "I stick with SMH," he wrote, explaining why he picked that fund over a rival ETF whose top holdings are those two chipmakers, according to TheStreet.

So why fold now? With volatility up and the market falling, Burry said puts tied to the AI buildout have become very expensive, which leaves outright short sales as his main bearish tool. He called shorting stocks "asymmetric the wrong way," and said his only remaining bearish options are on Palantir and MetLife, according to Bloomberg. He's also keeping plenty of dry powder. About 25% of his portfolio sits in cash. The rest is spread across stocks he considers undervalued, long-dated call options and preferred shares, which gives him room to buy if prices keep sliding.

Nvidia's comeback and the $200 line

Nvidia gave him a reason to stay nimble. The board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov. 23, and the stock jumped 31.48% to $165.05, its best single-day gain in more than two decades, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value, according to The Motley Fool. Few investors saw that kind of reversal coming just 11 days after Huang stepped down.

title: Trump Says Market Selloff Briefly Worried Him as He Defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

President Donald Trump said Wednesday's market decline briefly concerned him before indexes recovered much of their losses, while defending his role in returning Jensen Huang to the helm of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), according to comments to reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Thursday.

Trump called the market response to Huang's return positive but gave no evidence for his view that the executive poses no national security risk. Asked why he was confident, Trump cited information he did not identify. He said he had not spoken with Huang since the reinstatement but expected to do so before Monday.

Before the bell: Wall Street goes Black Friday shopping. Is Bitcoin on the list?
Natasha Ahmed

Trading disclosure

Wall Street didn't wait for the doors to open on Black Friday. Neither did crypto.

The largest cryptocurrency, Bitcoin (BTC), rose 1.7% to $61,698 early Friday.

Crypto stocks are moving even faster. Strategy Inc. (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, rose more than 5% in premarket trading, while Coinbase (COIN) gained 4.03%.

They're getting a lift from the rest of Wall Street. Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.32%, led by chip stocks, while S&P 500 futures gained 1.74%. Gold and silver are bouncing, too.

So is crypto the new black? Not quite yet.

Bitcoin has traded flat for the week and is still down about 33% from a year ago. Investors remain nervous. CoinGecko's Fear & Greed gauge sits at 22, in "extreme fear" territory.

Crypto fear and greed index. Source: CoinGecko

It also heads into the weekend with a warning sign on its chart. It also heads into the weekend with a warning sign on its chart.

Related: Bitcoin, XRP, Ethereum face brutal crash risk as key levels crack

Long live Bitcoin?

Peter Schiff, a longtime Bitcoin skeptic and gold advocate, marked Thanksgiving with a jab on X. He wrote that holders used to brag to family about a year of gains.

"But with a 33% YoY loss, it may be a sore subject this year," he wrote.

Peter Schiff's BTC take on Thanksgiving. Source: X

Schiff is no stranger to Bitcoin funerals. 

He has called Bitcoin dead 22 times, more than anyone else, according to BitcoinDeaths. Overall, Bitcoin has been declared dead 482 times since 2010, including 28 times this year, the tracker shows. 

A short day after a long week

Traders will have to move fast. U.S. markets close at 1 p.m. ET. for Black Friday.

The week started strongly after Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's CEO on Monday. Tariff worries and hot inflation data then weighed on risky assets. On Wednesday, investors briefly valued Strategy at less than the Bitcoin it holds, a record discount that JPMorgan analysts called a sign of "capitulation."

Bitcoin's price on every Black Friday from 2017 to 2026. Source: Coin Metrics; live price for 2026.

Related: Bitcoin crash can't shake asset manager's $1.6 million target

What to watch over the weekend?

Wall Street clocks out early today. Bitcoin doesn't.

That matters for investors who own Bitcoin through stocks like Strategy and Coinbase, or through Bitcoin ETFs. Regular trading in those shares ends at 1 p.m. today and resumes Monday. Bitcoin itself trades all weekend, so any big move is likely to show up in those shares at Monday's open.

Bitcoin's chart is also flashing a warning.

Bitcoin's 50-day exponential moving average has been below its 200-day average since mid-November, according to TradingView data, as seen on the CoinGecko website.

Bitcoin's 50-day EMA is below its 200-day EMA. Source:

On simple moving averages, which many traders also watch, the 50-day is still above the 200-day.

US stock index futures pointed to a sharply higher opening on Friday as trading resumed following the Thanksgiving holiday, with technology shares expected to extend their recent recovery amid continued market volatility.

Nasdaq 100 futures advanced 2.3%, reflecting renewed buying interest in technology companies following Wednesday's early sell-off.

Equity markets have experienced substantial fluctuations in recent sessions as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence investments, following the resignation and subsequent reinstatement of Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

"Investors will be counting their blessings that the pre-Thanksgiving recovery in global tech stocks looks like it's being sustained after the turkey has been cleared from people's plates," says AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould.

He added, "After a tumultuous week, there will be hopes this uptick can be sustained and that the momentum can carry over into the remainder of the year, despite worries about the sustainability of AI spending, rising borrowing costs and a renewed tariff threat."

Trading volumes could remain relatively subdued on Friday due to the shortened Wall Street session and the absence of major US economic releases.

Wall Street Recovers From Intraday Losses

US equities experienced another volatile session on Wednesday, recovering from substantial early losses to finish with mixed results.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 164.25 points, or 0.3%, to close at 50,182.95. The S&P 500 declined 18.31 points, or 0.3%, to 7,182.78, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 147.73 points, or 0.6%, to 23,585.80.

The Nasdaq had fallen as much as 4.6% earlier in the session as concerns surrounding artificial intelligence spending continued to weigh on technology stocks.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) closed nearly 4% lower, while Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) and Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) also recorded substantial declines.

"Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia removed an immediate source of uncertainty and helped lift the Nasdaq 100 nearly 7%, but Tuesday's losses and softer futures show that investors are reluctant to treat one powerful session as a turning point, with the index having given back a meaningful portion of the rebound," said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Financial Market Analyst at Capital.com.

"The issue is broader than Nvidia's leadership," she added. "Its shares fell back on Tuesday, while questions about AI spending, valuations and the returns companies can earn on their investment remain unresolved."

The open question is whether this marks the start of a recovery for beaten-down drone stocks or just a holiday bounce.

Ondas Pitches Cheap, Mass-Produced Autonomy

Ondas leadership is pitching a shift toward affordable, mass-produced autonomous systems. In a recent interview, Ondas Sentinel CEO Ryan Hartman said future warfare will rely on affordable autonomous systems powered by artificial intelligence and deployed in large numbers, adding, "for Ondas that's our sweet spot." Hartman also stated, "Everything we do, we're trying to bend the cost curve."
